key_insight: CCGE introduces an intrinsic exploration signal based on contact coverage that encourages a dexterous hand to discover diverse, meaningful hand–object contact modes, enabling general-purpose manipulation without task-specific reward engineering.
problem_solved: Dexterous manipulation suffers from sparse or ill-defined rewards and relies on handcrafted priors to shape hand–object interactions; CCGE addresses poor exploration and the lack of a general-purpose reward for discovering useful contact behaviors.
method: Represent contact state as a compact descriptor (e.g., contact map / contact patch set / contact graph) that summarizes which hand surfaces touch object surfaces.
Maintain a coverage memory / novelty estimator over contact descriptors and compute an intrinsic reward that increases when the agent generates previously under-covered contact states.
Integrate the intrinsic contact-coverage reward with standard DRL algorithms so agents learn diverse, transferable manipulation strategies without task-specific shaping.
impact: CCGE reduces the need for task-specific reward design and improves exploration and sample efficiency in sparse-reward dexterous tasks, making it easier for practitioners to train general-purpose manipulation skills transferable across objects and tasks.

paper_title: Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration for General-Purpose Dexterous Manipulation
paper_authors: Zixuan Liu, Ruoyi Qiao, Chenrui Tie, Xuanwei Liu, Yunfan Lou
